narrative.overview:
The page is one visible sheet of technical drawing paper. A hairline frame runs its full height, every section is a cell ruled off that frame, and crosshair ticks mark each place where two rules meet. On that sheet each project is a line drawing, plotted stroke by stroke rather than rendered: a broken ring, two overlapping circles (the second dotted), a roof over a square. One bright node dot travels a hairline orbit in the hero, and a faint gray bloom of light sits behind it. Nothing is filled except node dots and the inverted states.

The ink is strictly black, white and near-neutral gray. Dark (black sheet, white ink) and light (paper-white sheet, graphite ink) are peers. Neither is a fallback: the OS setting picks one before first paint, a `data-theme` attribute holds it, and the switch opens the new theme as a circular View Transition from the button that was pressed. The voice is Geist Mono, set large and tight, with Jost for reading and Doto dot-matrix kept to two sign-offs. Density is calm. Large mono headlines and wide cells sit against compact, tabular ledgers.

Two earlier worlds are confirmed anti-references: the frosted-glass lens over three filled primitives, and the older pixel world before it. Glass survives in exactly one place, the sticky nav.
keyCharacteristics: One hairline frame (1px side rails, max 1320px) with ruled cells and 13px crosshair ticks at every rule intersection.
A shared column rule (`--split`) that runs through the projects and about cells, ticked where it meets the cell rules.
Line-drawn primitives plotted by stroke-dashoffset on a normalised path length, each with a filled node dot.
Black, white and neutral gray only, in two peer themes.
Inversion as the interaction grammar: rows, tabs, pills and tools flip to text colour on the ground.
Geist Mono 500 with negative tracking as the display voice.

rules.name: The Ink-Only Rule
rules.body: No hue enters the system. Every value is black, white, or a gray within a few points of neutral. Project identity comes from the primitive's drawing, never from a colour.

rules.name: The Peer Themes Rule
rules.body: Every token has a dark and a light value, and both are designed. A new surface is not done until it reads correctly in both.

rules.name: The Mono Voice Rule
rules.body: Anything that names something (a headline, a project, a section, a key) is Geist Mono 500 with negative tracking. Jost reads, and it never names.

rules.name: The Two Stamps Rule
rules.body: Doto appears in exactly two places: the hero corner note and the footer sign. It is never used for headings, labels, or body copy.

rules.name: The Ticked Intersection Rule
rules.body: Wherever a horizontal rule meets the frame or the column rule, a 13px Ink 3 crosshair marks it. A new rule that spans the sheet gets its ticks.

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: Two-column cells divide at `split` so their dividers line up down the sheet. Don't invent a second column position.

rules.name: The One Pane Rule
rules.body: Glass exists only on the sticky nav. Panels, cards, tabs and overlays are opaque ground with a hairline edge.

rules.name: The Drawn Depth Rule
rules.body: If something needs to separate from the sheet, outline it or step its ground one tone. Never lift it with a shadow.

dos: **Do** put every new section in a cell on the frame: a 1px `line` top rule, `pad` padding, and crosshair ticks where the rule meets the rails or the `split` column.
**Do** draw any new project mark as a stroked primitive in a 100-unit box with `pathLength="1"`, a plot-in by stroke-dashoffset, and one filled node dot.
**Do** express hover and selection by inversion (text colour on the ground) or by a one-step ground lift, with 200 to 300ms ease-out (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`).
**Do** pair every primary action as a pill label plus a round arrow disc that rotates -45deg on hover. Use the hairline pill for the secondary.
**Do** set names, titles and labels in Geist Mono 500 with negative tracking, and running copy in Jost.
**Do** give every new colour a dark and a light value, and check both themes.
**Do** honour reduced motion: strokes render fully drawn, and orbit, dots and bloom stop.
donts: **Don't** use frosted glass anywhere but the sticky nav. The glass-lens and pane world is retired.
**Don't** fill a primitive or render it as a solid shape. Fills are reserved for node dots, status dots and inverted states.
**Don't** return to the pixel world. Doto's dot matrix is limited to the hero corner note and the footer sign.
**Don't** introduce hue, gradients beyond the gray bloom, or per-project accent colours.
**Don't** add drop shadows or offset shadows. Separate surfaces with hairlines and tonal steps.
**Don't** set small uppercase tracked labels above headings as eyebrows or kickers. Section titles carry their own `/path` name.
**Don't** use a system or Jost face for display text, or icon glyphs from fonts. Icons are inline SVG strokes.
